PullRequest.Title: Avoid reading large agent host files when opening Changes
PullRequest.Body:

Fixes #343103

## Problem

With a remote agent host, opening **Changes** in the Agents window for a repository with large untracked files (packet captures in the report) makes the agent host read each of those files in full and send it to the window as Base64. Its memory climbs by gigabytes until V8 runs out of heap and the process aborts, and reconnecting reopens Changes and crashes it again.

Reproduced locally with two 150 MiB and one 30 MiB untracked binary file: on `main` the agent host received a whole-file read request for all three files (330 MiB) as soon as Changes opened, its working set grew from about 164 MB to about 2.5 GB, and it crashed with `JavaScript heap out of memory` in 3 of 3 runs. With this change it reads none of them, peaks at about 208 MB, and does not crash (3 of 3 runs).

## Root cause

Opening Changes opens the session's Changes editor, a multi diff editor that resolves a text model for every changed file up front:

1. `SessionChangesEditor` resolves the input's view model when it is shown ([sessionChangesEditor.ts#L385-L386](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/cd2259bdf72ec7421e70ae80999ceb46f8bd86fe/src/vs/sessions/contrib/changes/browser/sessionChangesEditor.ts#L385-L386)), and `MultiDiffEditorInput._createModel` calls `ITextModelService.createModelReference` for both sides of every item ([multiDiffEditorInput.ts#L225-L230](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/cd2259bdf72ec7421e70ae80999ceb46f8bd86fe/src/vs/workbench/contrib/multiDiffEditor/browser/multiDiffEditorInput.ts#L225-L230)).
2. For a file-backed resource that resolves a text file model ([textModelResolverService.ts#L75-L77](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/cd2259bdf72ec7421e70ae80999ceb46f8bd86fe/src/vs/workbench/services/textmodelResolver/common/textModelResolverService.ts#L75-L77)). The text file service finds out that a file is binary from its first bytes and then cancels the read ([textFileService.ts#L224-L244](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/cd2259bdf72ec7421e70ae80999ceb46f8bd86fe/src/vs/workbench/services/textfile/browser/textFileService.ts#L224-L244)), but that only saves work when the file system can stream: for a provider without `FileReadStream` or `FileOpenReadWriteClose` the file service reads the whole file first ([fileService.ts#L624-L630](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/cd2259bdf72ec7421e70ae80999ceb46f8bd86fe/src/vs/platform/files/common/fileService.ts#L624-L630), [#L713](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/cd2259bdf72ec7421e70ae80999ceb46f8bd86fe/src/vs/platform/files/common/fileService.ts#L713)).
3. The agent host file system (`vscode-agent-host` URIs) only has `FileReadWrite` ([agentHostFileSystemProvider.ts#L173-L177](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/cd2259bdf72ec7421e70ae80999ceb46f8bd86fe/src/vs/platform/agentHost/common/agentHostFileSystemProvider.ts#L173-L177)), and `readFile` asks the host for the whole file with `resourceRead`, Base64-encoded ([#L493-L496](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/cd2259bdf72ec7421e70ae80999ceb46f8bd86fe/src/vs/platform/agentHost/common/agentHostFileSystemProvider.ts#L493-L496)). So detecting that an untracked capture is binary costs the host a full read, a Base64 string of the whole file and a message carrying it, for every such file at once.

The text and diff editors avoid this with a large file limit checked against a stat before reading ([resourceEditorInput.ts#L190-L209](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/cd2259bdf72ec7421e70ae80999ceb46f8bd86fe/src/vs/workbench/common/editor/resourceEditorInput.ts#L190-L209)), but the multi diff editor doesn't apply it, and `getLargeFileConfirmationLimit` gives agent host files the local limit of 1024 MB ([files.ts#L1632-L1659](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/cd2259bdf72ec7421e70ae80999ceb46f8bd86fe/src/vs/platform/files/common/files.ts#L1632-L1659)) although they are transferred like remote files.

## Fix

- `MultiDiffEditorInput`: for each side that comes from a file system that can only read whole files, stat it first (one `resourceResolve` round trip for the agent host) and compare the size with the large file limit that text editors use (`workbench.editorLargeFileConfirmation` when set, otherwise `getLargeFileConfirmationLimit`). When a side is above it, neither side is loaded and the item shows the existing binary placeholder with the label **File is too large to show**. File systems that stream reads (local disk, `vscode-remote`) are unchanged, since binary detection already stops after the first bytes there.
  - A side that already has a resolved text file model, such as a file that is open and dirty in an editor, is not checked: loading it reuses that model without reading the file, so it is shown, saved and reverted as before. If the other side of the item is too large, the item still shows the placeholder, and saving or reverting the multi diff editor still saves or reverts the item's dirty sides.
  - The check activates the file system provider first, as loading the model does, so a file system that an extension registers when it activates (for example when a multi diff editor is restored) is checked on the first load too. Untitled, in-memory and content provider resources are not read from a file system and are not checked.
- `getLargeFileConfirmationLimit`: agent host files (new `Schemas.vscodeAgentHost`, which `AGENT_HOST_SCHEME` now uses) get the remote limit of 10 MB. This also means a text editor opened on an agent host file over 10 MB asks before loading it, as for Remote-SSH files.

Deliberately unchanged:

- Files under the limit are still read in full to detect that they are binary (in the report, four captures between 1.9 and 5.4 MB, 12.8 MB together). The Base64 encoder's memory amplification for those reads is addressed separately by #339434, which complements this change.
- The original side of a modified tracked file is a git blob content reference without a size, so it is still loaded unless the working tree side is too large.
- No protocol, agent host or Changes view changes.

## Before / after

Both recordings: an Agents window connected through `chat.remoteAgentHosts` to a local agent host on a 2 GiB V8 heap, serving a repository with two 150 MiB and one 30 MiB untracked binary file and one edited README. The session is opened with Changes closed, then Changes is opened. The readout in the bottom-left corner is the scenario's own instrument: the agent host's working set, sampled from outside the process, and how many of the three large files the host was asked to read.

### Before

![Before: opening Changes leaves the Changes editor loading while the agent host's memory climbs past 1.7 GB, then the host process exits out of memory and the window shows Reconnecting](https://github.com/karthiknadig/vscode/blob/283442b2edb2708fb3597ef6367aac67b2482154/20261015-171820-C16-F1/before.gif?raw=true)

### After

![After: opening Changes lists the three captures as "File is too large to show" next to the README diff, and the agent host stays at about 160 MB with no large file read](https://github.com/karthiknadig/vscode/blob/283442b2edb2708fb3597ef6367aac67b2482154/20261015-171820-C16-F1/after.gif?raw=true)

## Measurements

What opening Changes costs the agent host, from a fresh agent host and a fresh Agents window per run. Reads were counted by wrapping `AgentService.resourceRead` in the agent host process. The working set was sampled every 200 ms from outside the process (Windows `Get-Process`; the peak is `PeakWorkingSet64`), because the host's event loop is blocked while it encodes a large file. Windows, Node.js 24.22.1, Code - OSS dev build with `VSCODE_DEV_DISABLE_DISPOSABLE_TRACKING=1`; the agent host is this build's `agentHostServerMain` with the scripted mock agent and `--max-old-space-size=2048` (a 2,240 MB V8 heap limit, close to the ~2 GiB limit in the report).

Two 150 MiB `.pcapng` files and one 30 MiB `.qmdl` file of random bytes, untracked, plus one edited README:

| | `main` @ `cd2259b` (3 runs) | This PR (3 runs) |
|---|---|---|
| Whole-file reads of the three large files requested by opening Changes | 3 per run (330 MiB) | none |
| Agent host working set with the session open and Changes closed | 163–164 MB | 164 MB |
| Agent host peak working set after opening Changes | 2,490–2,523 MB | 207–208 MB (the process's lifetime peak) |
| Agent host process crashed (`JavaScript heap out of memory`) | 3 of 3 | 0 of 3 |

The eight untracked files from the report, with the same sizes (358 MB in total, from 1.9 MB to 146 MB), one run each:

| | `main` @ `cd2259b` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Untracked files read in full when Changes opens | all 8 (358 MB requested) | the 4 under 10 MB (12.8 MB); the 4 over 10 MB are not read |
| Agent host peak working set | 2,490 MB | 723 MB |
| Agent host process crashed | yes | no (V8 heap peak 373 MB of 2,240 MB) |

These numbers are from the first version of this change, on `main` @ `cd2259b`, which is still its base. The later review fixes only change what happens for files that are already open in an editor and for file systems registered on demand; neither applies to these untracked files on the already-connected agent host, so the numbers were not measured again.

## How to test

1. Run a dev build of this branch and an agent host on a machine that has a git repository with a few large untracked binary files (for example `node -e "require('fs').writeFileSync('capture.pcapng', require('crypto').randomBytes(150*1024*1024))"` twice with different names) and one small edited file.
2. Connect the Agents window to that agent host (Remote-SSH, or `chat.remoteAgentHosts` pointing at a local agent host server), and open a session whose working directory is that repository, with Changes closed.
3. Open **Changes**. The large files appear with **File is too large to show**, the small file's diff appears, and the agent host's memory stays flat. On `main`, the agent host's memory climbs by several times the files' size and, with a 2 GiB heap, the agent host crashes.

<details><summary>Automated repro scenario</summary>

Start the instrumented agent host from the repository root with `node --max-old-space-size=2048 mockhost.mjs` (keep its stdin open; env `BS_STATUS` sets where it writes its read log and memory samples), create a session in the test repository with `node seed.mjs 8996 <repo>`, open an Agents window with `chat.remoteAgentHosts` set to `ws://127.0.0.1:8996` and `chat.agentHost.allowSignedOutWhenUsable` enabled, then run the scenario over CDP: `node <bug-swarm skill>/scripts/cdp-scenario.mjs --cdp <port> --scenario repro.cjs --out <dir>`. It fails on `main` and passes with this PR.

```js
// Repro: opening Changes in the Agents window must not make the agent host read large untracked files in full.
// Runs over CDP against an Agents window connected (chat.remoteAgentHosts) to the instrumented agent host in
// mockhost.mjs, which serves a git repository with three large untracked binaries (two 150 MiB .pcapng files and a
// 30 MiB .qmdl file) and one small tracked change (README.md). The host records every resourceRead and samples its
// own memory into BS_STATUS; a small overlay in the window shows the host's memory while the scenario runs.
const fs = require('fs');
const path = require('path');
const os = require('os');

const STATUS = process.env.BS_STATUS || path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'bs-changes-oom-status.json');
const LARGE_FILES = ['capture-1.pcapng', 'capture-2.pcapng', 'modem.qmdl'];
const ALL_FILES = ['README.md', ...LARGE_FILES];
const MAX_RSS_GROWTH_MB = 256;
const MiB = 1024 * 1024;

const readStatusOnce = () => { try { return JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(STATUS, 'utf8')); } catch { return undefined; } };
// The host rewrites the status file every 100 ms, so a read can see a partial file: retry briefly.
const readStatus = () => {
	for (let i = 0; i < 20; i++) {
		const s = readStatusOnce();
		if (s) { return s; }
		const until = Date.now() + 25;
		while (Date.now() < until) { /* wait */ }
	}
	return undefined;
};
const isAlive = pid => { try { process.kill(pid, 0); return true; } catch { return false; } };
const largeReads = s => (s?.reads ?? []).filter(r => r.uri.startsWith('file:') && LARGE_FILES.some(f => r.uri.endsWith('/' + f)));
const mb = n => `${Math.round(n)} MB`;

let baseline;
let overlayTimer;

async function waitFor(fn, timeoutMs, intervalMs = 200) {
	const end = Date.now() + timeoutMs;
	let value;
	while (Date.now() < end) {
		value = await fn();
		if (value) { return value; }
		await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, intervalMs));
	}
	return value;
}

// This repro needs no Copilot account: dismiss the sign-in prompt, which can open a few seconds after the window starts.
async function dismissSignIn(page) {
	for (let i = 0; i < 6; i++) {
		const cont = page.getByText('Continue Without Signing In');
		if (await cont.count()) { await cont.first().click(); await page.waitForTimeout(800); continue; }
		if (!await page.evaluate(() => !!document.querySelector('.monaco-dialog-box, .monaco-dialog-modal-block, .sessions-signing-in-dialog-modal-block'))) { break; }
		await page.keyboard.press('Escape');
		await page.waitForTimeout(800);
	}
}

// Small read-only readout of the agent host's memory in the bottom-left corner (the scenario's own instrument). It
// prefers BS_MEM, the working set sampled from outside the host, which keeps updating while the host's event loop is busy.
function startOverlay(page) {
	const update = async () => {
		const s = readStatusOnce();
		if (!s) { return; }
		let memMB = s.current.rssMB;
		try { memMB = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(process.env.BS_MEM, 'utf8')).samples.at(-1).wsMB; } catch { }
		const alive = isAlive(s.pid) && !s.exitedAt;
		const reads = largeReads(s);
		const text = alive
			? `Agent host memory: ${mb(memMB)} \u00b7 large files read: ${reads.length}`
			: `Agent host process exited (out of memory) \u00b7 large files read: ${reads.length}`;
		await page.evaluate(t => {
			let el = document.getElementById('bs-host-readout');
			if (!el) {
				el = document.createElement('div');
				el.id = 'bs-host-readout';
				el.style.cssText = 'position:fixed;left:12px;bottom:10px;z-index:100000;padding:4px 10px;border-radius:4px;font:12px var(--monaco-monospace-font, monospace);background:rgba(0,0,0,.75);color:#fff;pointer-events:none';
				document.body.appendChild(el);
			}
			el.textContent = t;
		}, text).catch(() => { });
	};
	overlayTimer = setInterval(update, 250);
	overlayTimer.unref?.();
	return update();
}

const changesEntries = page => page.evaluate(() => [...document.querySelectorAll('.multiDiffEntry')]
	.filter(e => e.offsetParent)
	.map(e => ({
		// The title also holds the +added/-removed stats; keep only the file label.
		name: (e.querySelector('.title.modified .label-name')?.textContent ?? e.querySelector('.title.modified')?.textContent ?? '').trim(),
		placeholder: (() => { const p = e.querySelector('.binary-file-placeholder'); return p && getComputedStyle(p).display !== 'none' ? p.querySelector('span')?.textContent.trim() : undefined; })(),
	})));

module.exports = {
	id: 'changes-large-untracked-files',
	title: 'Opening Changes does not read large untracked files on the agent host',
	source: 'https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/343103',
	stepPauseMs: 1200,
	steps: [
		{
			id: 'open-session', title: 'Open the session with Changes closed', async run({ page }) {
				const s = readStatus();
				if (!s || !isAlive(s.pid)) { throw new Error(`The agent host is not running (status ${STATUS})`); }
				await page.waitForFunction(() => [...document.querySelectorAll('.monaco-list-row')].some(r => (r.getAttribute('aria-label') || '').startsWith('hello')), null, { timeout: 60000 });
				await dismissSignIn(page);
				await page.locator('.monaco-list-row', { hasText: 'hello' }).first().click();
				await page.waitForFunction(() => [...document.querySelectorAll('.interactive-response')].some(e => e.textContent.includes('Hello, world!')), null, { timeout: 30000 });
				await dismissSignIn(page);
				await startOverlay(page);
				if ((await changesEntries(page)).length) { throw new Error('The Changes editor is already open'); }
				await page.waitForTimeout(2000);
				const now = readStatus();
				if (largeReads(now).length) { throw new Error(`The large files were read before Changes was opened: ${largeReads(now).length}`); }
				baseline = { rssMB: now.current.rssMB, heapUsedMB: now.current.heapUsedMB, reads: now.reads.length };
				return `Session open, Changes closed; agent host RSS ${mb(baseline.rssMB)}, V8 heap ${mb(baseline.heapUsedMB)}, no large file read yet`;
			}
		},
		{
			id: 'open-changes', title: 'Open Changes', async run({ page }) {
				fs.writeFileSync(STATUS + '.mark', JSON.stringify({ mark: 'open-changes' }));
				await page.waitForTimeout(300);
				await page.locator('a.codicon-diff-multiple').first().click();
				// Wait until every changed file is listed, or the agent host is gone.
				const outcome = await waitFor(async () => {
					const s = readStatus();
					if (s && (!isAlive(s.pid) || s.exitedAt)) { return 'host-exited'; }
					const names = (await changesEntries(page)).map(e => e.name);
					return ALL_FILES.every(f => names.some(n => n.startsWith(f))) ? 'listed' : undefined;
				}, 60000, 250);
				// Keep watching for a few seconds so late reads and the memory peak are captured.
				await page.waitForTimeout(4000);
				const entries = await changesEntries(page);
				return `After opening Changes: ${outcome ?? 'timed out'}; entries ${JSON.stringify(entries)}`;
			}
		},
		{
			id: 'check-host', title: 'The agent host read no large file and stayed within its memory budget', async run({ page }) {
				const s = readStatus();
				const reads = largeReads(s);
				const readBytes = reads.reduce((sum, r) => sum + (r.bytes ?? 0), 0);
				const alive = isAlive(s.pid) && !s.exitedAt;
				const peak = s.mark?.label === 'open-changes' ? s.peak : undefined;
				const summary = `large-file reads ${reads.length} (${reads.map(r => r.uri.split('/').pop()).join(', ') || 'none'}; ${Math.round(readBytes / MiB)} MiB returned), `
					+ `host RSS ${mb(baseline.rssMB)} -> peak ${peak ? mb(peak.rssMB) : '?'}, V8 heap peak ${peak ? mb(peak.heapUsedMB) : '?'} (limit ${s.heapLimitMB} MB), host ${alive ? 'alive' : 'EXITED'}`;
				clearInterval(overlayTimer);
				const problems = [];
				if (!alive) { problems.push('the agent host process exited'); }
				if (reads.length) { problems.push(`${reads.length} large untracked files were read in full`); }
				if (peak && peak.rssMB - baseline.rssMB > MAX_RSS_GROWTH_MB) { problems.push(`agent host RSS grew by ${mb(peak.rssMB - baseline.rssMB)} (budget ${MAX_RSS_GROWTH_MB} MB)`); }
				const entries = await changesEntries(page);
				const missing = ALL_FILES.filter(f => !entries.some(e => e.name.startsWith(f)));
				if (missing.length) { problems.push(`Changes does not list ${missing.join(', ')}`); }
				const notPlaceholder = LARGE_FILES.filter(f => !entries.find(e => e.name.startsWith(f))?.placeholder);
				if (!missing.length && notPlaceholder.length) { problems.push(`no placeholder for ${notPlaceholder.join(', ')}`); }
				if (problems.length) { throw new Error(`${problems.join('; ')}. ${summary}`); }
				return `${summary}; entries ${JSON.stringify(entries)}`;
			}
		},
	]
};
```

</details>

<details><summary>Instrumented agent host (mockhost.mjs)</summary>

```js
// Standalone Agent Host server (from a built VS Code checkout's out/) with the scripted mock agent, instrumented to
// show what opening Changes in the Agents window costs the host.
// - Wraps AgentService.resourceRead: records every read (uri, encoding, bytes returned, duration) in BS_STATUS.
// - Samples process.memoryUsage() every 100 ms and records the peak RSS and V8 heap since the last mark.
//   A client can set a mark by writing { "mark": "<label>" } to BS_STATUS + '.mark' (the host polls that file).
// Usage (from a shell that keeps stdin open; the server exits when stdin closes):
//   node [--max-old-space-size=N] mockhost.mjs   env: BS_VSCODE (checkout root), BS_PORT, BS_UDD, BS_STATUS
import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';
import path from 'node:path';
import fs from 'node:fs';
import os from 'node:os';
import v8 from 'node:v8';

const VSCODE = process.env.BS_VSCODE || process.cwd();
const out = p => pathToFileURL(path.join(VSCODE, 'out', p)).href;
const STATUS = process.env.BS_STATUS || path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'bs-changes-oom-status.json');
const MARK = STATUS + '.mark';
const MB = 1024 * 1024;

const status = {
	pid: process.pid,
	checkout: VSCODE,
	heapLimitMB: Math.round(v8.getHeapStatistics().heap_size_limit / MB),
	startedAt: Date.now(),
	mark: { label: 'start', at: Date.now() },
	reads: [],
	peak: { rssMB: 0, heapUsedMB: 0, externalMB: 0, at: 0 },
	current: {},
	marks: [],
};
let dirty = true;
const writeStatus = () => { if (dirty) { dirty = false; fs.writeFileSync(STATUS, JSON.stringify(status, null, 1)); } };
try { fs.unlinkSync(MARK); } catch { }

function sample() {
	const m = process.memoryUsage();
	const cur = { rssMB: Math.round(m.rss / MB), heapUsedMB: Math.round(m.heapUsed / MB), externalMB: Math.round((m.external + m.arrayBuffers) / MB), at: Date.now() };
	status.current = cur;
	if (cur.rssMB > status.peak.rssMB) { status.peak.rssMB = cur.rssMB; status.peak.at = cur.at; dirty = true; }
	if (cur.heapUsedMB > status.peak.heapUsedMB) { status.peak.heapUsedMB = cur.heapUsedMB; dirty = true; }
	if (cur.externalMB > status.peak.externalMB) { status.peak.externalMB = cur.externalMB; dirty = true; }
	try {
		const mark = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(MARK, 'utf8'));
		fs.unlinkSync(MARK);
		status.marks.push({ ...status.mark, peak: status.peak, reads: status.reads.length });
		status.mark = { label: mark.mark, at: Date.now() };
		status.peak = { ...cur };
		dirty = true;
	} catch { }
	dirty = true;
	writeStatus();
}
setInterval(sample, 100);
process.on('exit', () => { status.exitedAt = Date.now(); dirty = true; writeStatus(); });

const { AgentService } = await import(out('vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentService.js'));
const origRead = AgentService.prototype.resourceRead;
AgentService.prototype.resourceRead = async function (uri, encoding) {
	const entry = { uri: uri.toString(), encoding, startedAt: Date.now() };
	status.reads.push(entry);
	dirty = true;
	process.stderr.write(`[bs-host] resourceRead start ${entry.uri} (${encoding})\n`);
	try {
		const result = await origRead.call(this, uri, encoding);
		entry.resultChars = result?.data?.length ?? 0;
		entry.bytes = result?.encoding === 'base64' ? Math.floor(entry.resultChars * 3 / 4) : Buffer.byteLength(result?.data ?? '');
		return result;
	} catch (e) {
		entry.error = String(e?.message ?? e).slice(0, 200);
		throw e;
	} finally {
		entry.ms = Date.now() - entry.startedAt;
		dirty = true;
		process.stderr.write(`[bs-host] resourceRead done ${entry.uri} bytes=${entry.bytes ?? '-'} ms=${entry.ms}${entry.error ? ' error=' + entry.error : ''}\n`);
	}
};

process.argv = [process.argv[0], process.argv[1], '--enable-mock-agent', '--port', process.env.BS_PORT || '8996', '--host', '127.0.0.1', '--without-connection-token', '--quiet', '--user-data-dir', process.env.BS_UDD || path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'bs-changes-oom-ahost-udd')];
await import(out('vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentHostServerMain.js'));
setInterval(() => { }, 1 << 30);
```

</details>

// host at <port>, runs one "hello" turn so it has a transcript, and prints the session URI.

import path from 'node:path';

globalThis._VSCODE_FILE_ROOT = path.join(VSCODE, 'out');

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed loop, both concrete Agent Host RPC implementations, the existing FileService validation stat, and the all-documents await are directly traced. Exact network latency and typical change-set size vary, which affects severity but not the duplicated boundary mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Agent Host resourceResolve RPCs and remote filesystem stat operations
Findings.PerformanceScaling: On a cold multi-diff with N changed resources, this adds up to one preflight stat for each original and modified URI (up to 2N calls); all are launched without a limiter, and each small file then incurs the existing validation stat again.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased Changes-editor open latency, extra remote I/O, and a burst of metadata RPCs
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Each side immediately created its model reference. The ensuing FileService.readFileStream path started its existing validateReadFile resolve/stat and the resourceRead concurrently, so a small Agent Host file paid one metadata RPC and one content RPC without a serialized preflight round trip.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The added per-item Promise.all calls _isTooLargeToLoad for both sides before createModelReference. For whole-file providers that helper awaits IFileService.stat; when the file is below the limit, createModelReference then reaches FileService.validateReadFile, which resolves/stats the same resource a second time before the item can finish.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 265 newly invokes _isTooLargeToLoad for every original URI (with line 266 doing the same for modified URIs) before the unchanged model-reference load; this is the added first stat stage that did not exist before the PR.
Findings.Title: Reuse the preflight stat when loading small files
Findings.Impact: Opening Changes for a realistic remote change set of tens or hundreds of ordinary files now waits for an extra Agent Host round trip before any of those files starts loading, while doubling metadata RPCs per cold URI. The outer Promise.all also makes the entire view-model initialization wait for the slowest duplicated chain.
Findings.Evidence: The added calls at lines 265-266 run inside mapObservableArrayCached for every diff item, and line 248 awaits _fileService.stat. The provider implements stat as an Agent Host resourceResolve request, while model resolution reads through TextFileService/FileService; FileService.doReadFileStream always starts validateReadFile, whose resolve performs another provider stat, alongside provider.readFile/resourceRead. updateDocuments awaits Promise.all of all item promises, so this work is on the editor-open critical path.
Findings.Recommendation: Preserve the large-file guard but pass/reuse the preflight metadata in the subsequent model/file read, or coalesce the immediate validation stat with it, so small files perform one resolve/stat and do not serialize their read behind a redundant round trip.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: The old multi-diff mapper eagerly created a text-model reference for every side. AgentHostFileSystemProvider only exposes whole-file FileReadWrite, so its readFile issues resourceRead for the complete file, whose server implementation reads the full file and returns it base64-encoded; binary detection and size validation therefore occurred only after transferring and allocating the whole payload.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Opening Changes with an oversized Agent Host file could transfer, base64 encode/decode, and allocate the entire remote file before showing it as binary, causing long open latency and high memory/GC pressure (the added regression test models a 150 MB file).
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The new preflight size check classifies oversized resources and the condition on line 271 skips createModelReference for both sides, avoiding the whole-file resourceRead and showing a placeholder instead.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: Base line 225 created a model reference unconditionally for every defined URI. The traced provider path is createModelReference -> TextFileService.readStream -> FileService.readFileStream -> AgentHostFileSystemProvider.readFile -> resourceRead; FileSystemResources.read uses IFileService.readFile and returns the complete encoded payload. Added tests assert that a 150 MB Agent Host resource is not loaded, while an 80-byte resource still is.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open an SCM/chat Changes multi-diff backed by Agent Host or another whole-file provider
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Resolve the multi-diff source, map every resource, await original/modified size checks, create model references for non-large items, await all document promises, then publish the view model. The preflight stat and each small-file model load are on the editor-open critical path; no document list is published until the slowest item completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Preflight resource metadata lookup via IFileService.stat -> AgentHostFileSystemProvider.stat -> resourceResolve -> remote filesystem stat
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to one call per unresolved whole-file original/modified URI, at most 2N for N two-sided items; calls are not grouped or limited.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No separate preflight; model loading began immediately.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each URI's content/model load is serialized behind this result, and the editor awaits every item.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read-time metadata validation via FileService.validateReadFile -> resolve/stat -> Agent Host resourceResolve
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One per small unresolved side loaded through the file service; no grouping. After the diff this duplicates the preflight stat for each such side.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This was the only metadata lookup and was started concurrently with content reading.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs during model resolution and must complete before the file content object is returned.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Whole-file Agent Host content RPC via resourceRead, including full-file read and base64 encode/decode
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One per small unresolved side; oversized sides now perform zero reads after one preflight stat.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One whole-file transfer for every unresolved side, including oversized files.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Small-file model creation waits for the content. Oversized-file transfer is removed from the critical path by this diff.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N distinct resource-pair keys in the change set, with up to 2N unique original/modified URIs after accounting for absent sides and already-resolved text models.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: mapObservableArrayCached starts one async mapper per resource; each mapper starts both side checks with Promise.all, and updateDocuments awaits all mappers with Promise.all. There is no shared limiter, so up to two cold preflight stats per item burst concurrently; model validation stats and reads begin as individual preflights complete.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A resolved text-file model bypasses the preflight and is reused. mapObservableArrayCached retains work for unchanged URI-pair keys while the source remains live, so resource-list updates only pay for new keys. Cold unresolved whole-file resources pay the new preflight; small resources then pay the existing validation stat. Failed preflights are not negatively cached beyond the current mapped promise and fall through to model loading.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added per-side calls, provider RPC, existing read-time stat, unlimited Promise.all scheduling, and final all-documents await are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual change-set size and Agent Host round-trip latency vary, but tens to hundreds of changed files are realistic; uncertainty affects severity, not the proven duplicate RPC and serialized stage.
Scenarios.Verdict: The oversized-file branch is a concrete performance fix, but ordinary small cold files regress from one concurrent stat/read pair to a preflight stat followed by another stat/read pair. A medium boundary-fanout finding was submitted.

Scenarios.Scenario: Save or revert a multi-diff containing a too-large item whose other side is already open and dirty
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The explicit save/revert command scans current items, checks dirty state for the two URIs of a too-large binary placeholder, invokes the text-file save/revert operations, and waits for all selected operations before completing the command.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Text-file save or revert for an already-resolved dirty URI
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one operation per dirty original/modified URI, up to 2K URI positions across K items; clean and untitled URIs are filtered.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The normal loaded diff branch already saved/reverted dirty original and modified models concurrently; the new branch preserves that behavior when an opposite oversized side prevents creating the diff model.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The user-initiated save/revert command waits for all selected operations.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: K dirty, resolved URIs among too-large placeholder items; unresolved large files are excluded by isDirty and perform no write.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All items are processed with Promise.all, and up to two dirty URIs per too-large item are also processed with Promise.all. There is no new limiter, but this mirrors the pre-existing all-item save/revert concurrency for loaded text diff models.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Dirty/resolved model state is the gate. There is no new cache; text-file services own model and write coalescing.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for call placement and cardinality; low prevalence does not change the mechanism.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: It is uncommon for one side to be oversized while another side is simultaneously open and dirty, and actual provider write cost varies.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the new operations only restore save/revert behavior for resolved dirty models that would otherwise be skipped, and do not increase concurrency relative to the existing all-item save path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render and scroll virtualized multi-diff placeholders for binary and oversized files
Scenarios.CriticalPath: For each materialized virtualized row, the reactive render reads item state, selects the localized placeholder label, updates textContent and aria-label, and toggles existing editor/placeholder display state. Work is confined to visible/materialized rows.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of visible/materialized diff rows and reactive rerenders, not total repository file count because the item template is virtualized.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous browser DOM updates occur per rendered virtualized item; there are no subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network calls on this path.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Localized label strings are created once per template instance; no remote cache applies. Existing observable/virtualization ownership controls rerenders and row lifetime.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed hunk is direct DOM assignment inside the existing item autorun.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact rerender frequency depends on scrolling and observable changes, but the added work is two small property updates per materialized row.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression: the added label updates are bounded by virtualization and do not introduce layout reads, full-tree work, retained state, or expensive boundaries.
